title: The Frohmanian Symplectic Tether $\T$:\\ Written Proofs Companion to the Lean~4 Formalization

claims.statement: $\T[\kappa,w,u](F,G):=-(\kappa w)\ip{\Pi_uF}{\Pi_uG}$. \LeanRef{Frohman.Tether.frohmanianTether; frohmanianTether_apply}

(a) $\T$ is symmetric. (b) $\T(F,F)\le0$ whenever $\kappa w\ge0$. (c) It is degenerate with respect to the kinetic-energy gradient: $\T(F,u)=0$ for all $F$. (d) It is invariant under every isometry commuting with $\Pi_u$.
claims.title: Basic properties

claims.statement: Let $B$ be a symmetric bilinear form that is (C1) invariant under the coadjoint isometries fixing $u$ and (C2) degenerate with respect to $u$. Then $B=\T[c,1,u]$ for some $c\in\mathbb R$. If, in addition, (C3) fixes the coefficient ($C3(\T[c,1,u])\Rightarrow c=\kappa w$), then $B=\T[\kappa,w,u]$.
claims.title: Uniqueness up to scale

claims.statement: Let $\omega\perp u$, $\|\omega\|=1$, $w\neq0$. Suppose $\T[\kappa,w,u]$ matches the stretching coefficient $S$ in the sense $\T[\kappa,w,u](\omega,\omega)+S w=0$. Then $\kappa=S$. Consequently, in $\dim\ge3$ with $S\ge0$, $w>0$, a correction is admissible for Route~A iff $B=\T[\kappa,w,u]$ with $\kappa=S$.
claims.title: Route A determines $\kappa$

claims.statement: For a classical (Jacobi) bracket $P$ and the tethered bracket $P+\T$, the Jacobiator expands into nine terms. The three purely classical ones cancel by Jacobi of $P$, and the three purely tether terms vanish. So the Jacobiator equals the cyclic sum of the mixed terms, and Jacobi holds on a set $R$ iff that cyclic sum vanishes on $R$. It vanishes when $u$ is central for $P$, $P$ is homogeneous in its first slot, and $\Pi_u P(a,b)=0$.
claims.title: Nine-term Jacobi

claims.statement: Every bilinear form splits uniquely into symmetric and antisymmetric parts. $\T$ is purely symmetric, and the metriplectic bracket $P+\T$ with $P$ antisymmetric conserves kinetic energy: $\{E,E\}=0$ and $\T(F,\nabla E)=0$.
claims.title: Metriplectic split

claims.statement: (a) $d_2\circ d_1=0$ on 1-cochains of any Lie algebra. (b) Coboundaries are cocycles. (c) If $2$ is invertible and the symmetric part of $\beta$ is alternating, it is zero. So a nonzero symmetric correction such as $\T$ is never a CE 2-cochain.
claims.title: Chevalley--Eilenberg

claims.statement: $\mathrm{div}(\sin y,0,0)\equiv0$, whereas $\mathrm{div}(\sin x,0,0)=\cos x$, which equals $1$ at the origin.
claims.title: $T^3$ shear

claims.statement:
•[(a)] The field bracket satisfies Jacobi. So the Arnold (Lie--Poisson) bracket on linear functionals is classical. •[(b)] If $\langle u,uangle
eq0$, the Jacobiator of the tethered bracket equals the cyclic sum of the mixed terms $[T(a,b),c]+T([a,b],c)$. •[(c)] Divergence-free fields along $e_x$ (parallel shears $f(y,z)e_x$) commute pairwise. Hence at $u=(\sin y,0,0)$ the mixed terms cancel, and Jacobi holds, for every triple in that class. •[(d)] At $u=(\sin x,0,0)$, which is not divergence-free, take the divergence-free triple $a=b=c=(1,0,0)$. The $e^{ix}$, $x$-component coefficient of the mixed sum is $	frac32\kappa w$. So Jacobi fails whenever $\kappa w
e0$. •[(e)] At $u=(\sin y,0,0)$ with the divergence-free triple $a=b=c=(0,0,\sin x)$, the $e^{i(x+y)}$, $z$-component coefficient is $	frac{3i}{8}\kappa w
eq0$. So Jacobi fails here too.
claims.title: Field-level Jacobi

claims.statement:
If $(u,p)$ is a classical smooth solution of $\partial_tu+(u\cdot
abla)u=-
abla p+
u\Delta u+F$ with $\mathrm{div}\,u=0$, then $\omega=\mathrm{curl}\,u$ satisfies $\partial_t\omega+(u\cdot
abla)\omega=(\omega\cdot
abla)u+
u\Delta\omega+\mathrm{curl}\,F$.
claims.title: Curl of forced NS

claims.statement: For each nonzero wavevector $k$ and amplitude $a\perp k$, the mode $b=\frac{ik\times a}{|k|^2}e^{ik\cdot x}$ satisfies $\mathrm{curl}\,b=a\,e^{ik\cdot x}$ and $\mathrm{div}\,b=0$, and it is the unique such divergence-free mode. Summing gives a right inverse of curl on mean-zero divergence-free trigonometric polynomials.
claims.title: Biot--Savart on trigonometric polynomials

claims.statement: If $\mathrm{curl}^{-1}$ is a right inverse of curl on the admissible class containing $-\kappa P(|\omega|^2\omega)$, then every velocity solution of the tethered NS solves \eqref{eq:tv}.
claims.title: Velocity form $\Rightarrow$ vorticity form

claims.statement: If $P$ is a symmetric idempotent and $P\omega=\omega$, then $\ip{\omega}{-\kappa Pg}=-\kappa\ip{\omega}{g}$. With $g=|\omega|^2\omega$ this equals $-\kappa\|\omega\|_4^4$.

Let $E=\tfrac12\|\omega\|_2^2$ and $Q=\|\omega\|_4^4$. Assume $E'=S-\nu D-\kappa Q$ (Cited Prop.~\ref{cp:EI}), $S\le C\sqrt{2E}\sqrt Q$ (Cited Prop.~\ref{cp:CZ}), and $(2E)^2\le Q$ (Cited Prop.~\ref{cp:Holder}). Then for $\kappa>0$, $E(t)\le\max(E_0,\,C^2/(2\kappa^2))$ on $[0,T]$.
For $\omega\in\mathbb R^3$ and $D=\nabla\omega$, $\sum_{ij}D_{ij}\,\partial_j(|\omega|^2\omega_i)=|\omega|^2|D|^2+\tfrac12\sum_j(2\sum_k\omega_kD_{kj})^2\ge0$, with no alignment assumption.
claims.title: Tether is sign-definite at $H^1$

claims.statement:
Let $G=\|
abla\omega\|_2^2$, $L=\|\Delta\omega\|_2$. Assume $G'=2(-
u L^2-\kappa J+N)$ with $J\ge0$ (Cited Prop.~ef{cp:H1I}) and $N\le A\,G^{1/4}L^{3/2}$ (Cited Prop.~ef{cp:NL}). Then $G(t)\le G(0)\exp\! ig(	frac{27A^4}{16
u^3}t ig)$.

Assume the tethered log inequality (Cited Prop.~\ref{cp:NSlog}), higher-norm control, BKM continuation (Cited Prop.~\ref{cp:BKM}) and local continuation (Cited Prop.~\ref{cp:LC}). Then the solution is smooth on $[0,T]$ for every $T$. Higher-norm control is itself discharged by Theorems~\ref{thm:L2} and \ref{thm:H1} together with Cited Prop.~\ref{cp:boot}.
claims.title: Global smoothness of the tethered system, conditional

claims.statement: Integrated enstrophy identity for \eqref{eq:tv}. It follows from multiplying by $\omega$, integrating by parts on $T^3$, and the lemma above.
claims.title: \lean{TetheredEnstrophyIdentity}

claims.statement: $\int\omega\cdot S\omega\le C\|\omega\|_2\|\omega\|_4^2$: Calder\'on--Zygmund / Biot--Savart, classical.
claims.title: \lean{StrainL2Bound}

claims.statement: $\|\omega\|_2^4\le\|\omega\|_4^4$ on the unit-volume torus (H\"older). \textbf{Now proved} for every probability space with $E=\tfrac12\int g$, $Q=\int g^2$, $g=|\omega|^2\in L^2$ (\lean{l4l2Holder_of_prob}, via nonnegativity of variance).
claims.title: \lean{L4L2Holder}

claims.statement: The $H^1$ energy identity (Majda--Bertozzi~\cite{MB} \S3.2 for the NS part).
claims.title: \lean{TetheredH1Identity}

claims.statement: Sobolev/Gagliardo--Nirenberg bound of the nonlinear term~\cite{Temam,CF}.
claims.title: \lean{NonlinH1Bound}

claims.statement: $H^1$ bounds on $[0,T)$ imply $H^s$ bounds for all $s$. For plain NS this is classical parabolic regularity~\cite{Temam,CF,MB}. \textbf{The tether-specific step (controlling $\kappa P(|\omega|^2\omega)$ in $H^s$, which is plausible since $H^2\subset L^\infty$ in 3D) is not in the literature and remains to be proved.}
claims.title: \lean{H1ToHsBootstrap}

claims.statement: Pointwise evolution at the maximum, and stretching $\le\|S\|_\infty y^2$.
claims.title: \lean{EnergyIdentity}, \lean{StretchingByStrain}

claims.statement: $\|S\|_\infty\le C(1+\|\omega\|_2+\|\omega\|_\infty\log(e+\|\omega\|_{H^s}))$~\cite{BKM}; see also Brezis--Gallou\"et and Kozono--Taniuchi~\cite{KT}.
claims.title: \lean{BKMLogInequality}

claims.statement: The cross term at the maximum is absorbed with constant $C_{abs}$.
claims.title: \lean{CrossControlled}

claims.statement: The integrated (time-continuous) form of the pointwise inequality along the solution.
claims.title: \lean{NSTetherLogInequality}, \lean{NSTetherEnstrophyInequality}

claims.statement: Beale--Kato--Majda~\cite{BKM}: bounded $\|\omega\|_\infty$ on $[0,T)$ implies continuation. Stated for plain NS; its extension to \eqref{eq:tv} is assumed.
claims.title: \lean{BKMContinuation}

claims.statement: Local existence for smooth periodic data (Fujita--Kato~\cite{FK}, Kato~\cite{Kato}).
claims.title: \lean{LocalContinuation}

claims.statement: Proved on trigonometric polynomials. The extension to the smooth admissible class requires a density/continuity argument not yet formalized.
claims.title: \lean{CurlRightInverse} beyond trigonometric polynomials

Its title is “\lean{StrainL2Bound}”, which does not appear to describe that statement. Is the title or the statement misworded?
cd0bdcad3c76.answer: harmless wording (strict, mechanical): the title cites Lean name(s) StrainL2Bound, each an existing declaration mapped to this claim; the title makes no further assertion.
